_contract: The canonical owner of this investigation's COSTS. The ceiling is owned by authorization.json, which this file points at. scripts/pod/batch_invariance_budget.py reads both and derives the session limit; the launcher carries no copy of any of it, because two places holding the same number is how one of them comes to be wrong. Read before each paid action. A rerun does NOT reset it and a replacement resource does NOT receive a fresh allocation.
_authorization_is_a_PATH_not_an_object: derive_budget.engineering_campaigns resolves `granted_utc` by reading this field as a relative path. An inline object leaves the date unresolved, the attribution `unknown`, and `full_ceiling_sessions_fundable` correctly refusing to answer -- which is what the first draft of this file did.
_the_ceiling_is_NOT_restated_here: It lives in authorization.json and nowhere else. This file held a copy, and while two ceilings are equal a gate reading either one passes every test; the copy is only discovered when they diverge, which is the moment it matters.
_inherited_total_is_derived: 0.0822, recomputed from the four components above rather than copied from the prior campaign's stated total. A roll-up total has silently dropped $0.0073 in this project before.
_teardown_reserve: Held back from every session ceiling so a teardown can always be paid for. RunPod's --terminate-after backstop has never been observed to fire in this project, so teardown is a verification poll, not an assumption.

subruns.cost_basis: wall clock from pod creation to confirmed teardown x quoted secure rate, plus container disk billed separately
subruns.failure: the image's python has torch and no huggingface_hub, and every input arrives through it; the relay fetch raised ModuleNotFoundError 4 seconds into the payload
subruns.second_defect: `scp -r host:/workspace/out/.` is the old idiom and the SFTP-backed scp in current OpenSSH refuses it -- 'error: unexpected filename: .'. It fetched nothing. There was nothing to fetch this time, which is the only reason it cost no evidence.
subruns.repair: pin-install huggingface_hub[hf_transfer]==1.23.0 into the image python before any fetch -- the wheelhouse's own version, a bootstrap dependency and not part of any measured environment; and copy the DIRECTORY rather than its dot-entry
subruns.watchdog: started, pid 3344959, stopped by the trap after teardown

rate_basis._field: securePrice, NOT communityPrice. The launcher prices on securePrice and a report that quoted $0.79 from communityPrice was acted on by a maintainer once.
rate_basis._disk_is_billed_separately: A GPU-only ceiling once missed $1.69 of container disk and nothing in that record disagreed.

_how_the_launcher_uses_this: scripts/pod/batch_invariance_budget.py sums inherited_spend plus every subruns[].cost_usd, subtracts that from authorization.json's all_in_ceiling_usd, subtracts teardown_reserve_usd, FLOORS the result to the cent, caps it at one session's worth, and reports `ok: no` when what remains cannot fund a useful attempt. The launcher refuses on `no`; it does not re-decide.
_inherited_spend_is_NOT_summed_by_derive: Deliberate. derive_budget.engineering_campaigns sums `subruns` only, and those four subruns are already booked on the batching-refactor-cuda campaign record it also discovers. They appear here so THIS investigation's $3.00 ceiling sees them, and nowhere else, so the project book counts them exactly once.
